title: Union fines for working under scale end Hayes's career
summary: Ramsey reported them to the union; each man was fined $50 and Hayes $500, which took him out of music and left Harlan Leonard the band.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Well, what did Ramsey figure to win by
I don't know. He was foreign to us, he was from Chicago and we were Kansas City -- most of us were from Kansas City people
Somebody had to contact -- or well he contacted somebody?
We met him in Chicago when the band was playing in Chicago.
He must have struck up a friendship with Thamon?

Well, he did. Thamon thought it would be a great thing to have him in front of the band. In fact, he stood in front of the band with tails and a high collar and all this bit, you know, just like a big time director and it looked good but we had no idea that he would do something like this. See this was a setback to the band.
So the union accused Thamon, I would guess, of playing under scale, was that the charge?

Yes, but we all were fined. I'm thinking that each individual was fined $50.00 and Thamon Hayes was fined $500, which he couldn't raise and I doubt whether all of us together could have helped him raise it. Things were just that tough. So that's what took Thamon out of
And it was then that Harlan Howlin Leonard took over the band?
Harlan Howlin Leonard took over the band and which his mother-in-law had staked--
Well, did you guys pay your fines?
We had to, oh yeah, we had to. We didn't have to pay it right on the spot but we could pay it in payments, which we all did.
